source_review.notes: Checked six official/primary sources. Microsoft supports the distinct circuit-breaker and bulkhead purposes and the closed/open/half-open model. Google SRE supports overload, cascading-failure, early-rejection, graceful-degradation, retry-control, and overload-testing claims. Envoy documentation supports cluster circuit-breaking resource limits and distinct endpoint outlier ejection. Resilience4j documentation confirms that CircuitBreaker, Bulkhead, Retry, RateLimiter, and TimeLimiter are separate composable controls. Product mechanisms are attributed and not generalized beyond their documented scope.

evidence: Checked eligible counts n/f/s, minimum count n_min, rate thresholds theta_f/theta_s, permits P, interval T_o, generation g, concurrency I/C, queue Q/Q_max, arrival rate lambda, residence W, and occupancy L for consistent meanings.
Confirmed breaker-rate ratios have nonzero denominator because evaluation follows minimum volume.
Confirmed bounded-occupancy and fleet-probe statements distinguish local from aggregate scope.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Little's Law is explicitly presented as a stable-system measurement relationship, not a capacity guarantee.

evidence: Recomputed 12 failures among 20 eligible calls as 60%, above the 50% example threshold.
Recomputed 500 requests/s times 0.2 s as 100 mean in flight and times 1 s as 500, leaving 350 beyond a 150-permit cap.
Recomputed 800 requests/s times 0.15 s as 120 and times 0.9 s as 720.
Recomputed 100 clients times five probes as 500 and tenant reserve as 100 minus 20 equals 80; counted ten examples, five exercises, and five answers.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All capacities and thresholds are labeled scenarios requiring load evidence before production use.

evidence: Derived I<=C from atomic admission, one permit per admitted call, and exactly-once release while noting resources outside the permit are unbounded by the proof.
Derived open-state call suppression from ordinary-call rejection plus bounded probes and identified hidden call paths as a counterexample.
Constructed the per-instance recovery counterexample showing that local P does not bound fleet traffic.
Checked that rate, concurrency, residence time, queue length, and queue age are separate constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The arguments state their scope and do not claim availability or correctness from admission controls alone.

evidence: Reviewed zero/low traffic, threshold oscillation, slow success, abrupt failure, gradual slowdown, intermittent failure, stuck calls, cancellation, late prior-generation results, and cold recovery.
Reviewed endpoint, service, region, method, tenant, credential, per-process, fleet, and shared-downstream scopes.

Reviewed empty/full/aged queues, permit leaks/double release, blocking versus nonblocking execution, autoscaling multiplication, restart, configuration rollout, telemetry loss, and manual override expiry.
Reviewed noisy tenants, high-cardinality keys, endpoint-ejection cascade, fallback exhaustion, forged/fabricated success, sensitive metrics, and timeout-after-commit ambiguity.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes correctness, resource, timing, topology, recovery, operational, and hostile-input boundaries.

evidence: Confirmed ordinary calls cannot reach an open circuit and half-open probes cannot exceed the declared effective budget.
Confirmed in-flight and queued work remain bounded only when admission is atomic and every terminal path releases exactly once.
Confirmed ineligible business/caller outcomes do not corrupt dependency failure rate.
Confirmed retries reacquire admission, preserve the original deadline and identity, and receive no privileged bypass.
Confirmed fallback, failover, endpoint ejection, and circuit state do not create authority or outcome certainty.
invariant_checking.notes: The module consistently separates dependency evidence, resource admission, routing, and overload rejection.

evidence: Reviewed occupancy proof and confirmed it bounds only resources represented by permits.
Reviewed circuit-suppression proof and confirmed hidden retry/client paths invalidate the claimed bound.
Reviewed tenant-isolation proof and confirmed a shared resource can remain a common-mode counterexample.
Reviewed recovery counterexample and confirmed deterministic per-instance timers can violate fleet capacity.
proof_review.notes: Claims are bounded, conditional, and paired with explicit counterexamples.

evidence: Confirmed the four arguments are labeled by purpose and list assumptions or invalidating cases.
Confirmed library/product behavior is attributed to Microsoft, Envoy, Resilience4j, or Google rather than presented as a universal protocol.
Confirmed proposed ordering, thresholds, and limits are design examples rather than external standards.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No empirical capacity claim is presented as a theorem.

evidence: All six official/primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current product guidance applies.
All call rates, durations, thresholds, permit counts, tenant shares, host counts, and probe counts are explicitly examples or candidate configurations.

Safe concurrency, latency thresholds, window sizes, recovery rates, fallback capacity, endpoint headroom, resource-per-call, fairness, and autoscaling effects remain explicit load/fault/integration evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production dependency, fleet, service mesh, or workload was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed circuit identity, eligibility classification, windows, hysteresis, state transitions, recovery, bulkhead boundaries, sizing, execution models, composition, topology, fallback, security, telemetry, and fault verification as distinct but interacting controls.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through operation decision tables, bounded keys, generation-safe transitions, deadline-aware atomic permits, bounded/aged queues, explicit decorator order, per-attempt admission, aggregate probe budgets, progressive recovery, protected fallback, reason-coded metrics, and adversarial fault/load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module moves from control separation and semantic evidence through state and recovery, then resource isolation, composition, topology, fallback, security, observation, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
